messages:
maya: Heads-up — rolling out updated deploy guardrails and a small quiet-window shift for this release train. TL;DR: reduced release freeze to 3h (previously 6h), introduced a lightweight exemption flow, and mandatory canary rollouts for model or infra changes that affect >5% traffic. See the short bullets below and the link to the full doc.
deploy-bot: Scheduled quiet window updated: Fri 21:00–00:00 UTC (previously 22:00–01:00). Auto-scheduling applied to all services tagged `release-train`.
liam (eng): Quick q — if we have an urgent security hotfix that needs to go in during the quiet window, do we use the exemption flow or emergency deploy docs? :thinking:
maya: Use the exemption flow first — it's faster and logged. If it's a true emergency (infra down / P0), follow the emergency deploy playbook and @oncall. Exemption flow: `/deploy-exempt --service <svc> --env prod --reason "<short reason>" --owner @<you>` will route to release-manager + SRE for a 15m review.
olivia (product): For the model change rule (">5% traffic"), does that include embedding-only endpoints? wondering about rolling a quantized model for embeddings.
maya: Yes, traffic % is by endpoint. Embeddings count. For embedding-model swaps expected to change latency or cost >5%, start a canary and open an eval snapshot in the PR. If it's pure config tweak with no model artifact change, note it in the exemption request.
jade (sre): Heads-up — alert thresholds for canary failures have been lowered during quiet windows (to detect regressions earlier). We're also enabling a short-lived synthetic load check for canaries: 5m smoke then 30m steady-state. :eyes:
jon (release-manager): Canary cadence we're enforcing: 10% traffic for 30m -> 50% for 15m -> full. If any smoke or SLO regression appears, auto-rollback triggers (we've tested the rollback path). If teams want a custom cadence, add justification to the exemption request.
maya: Exact rollout config in the handbook: https://redwood.internal/handbook/deploy-guardrails (doc includes examples and the `/deploy-exempt` template). Quick example exemption command for a hotfix proof:
```bash
/deploy-exempt --service inference-api --env prod --reason "latency encoder hotfix" --owner @liam --expected-risk "low" 
```
deploy-bot: Policy change logged: deploy-guardrails v2.1 applied to org=redwood. Audit: https://redwood.internal/audit/2026-03-deploy-guardrails
emma (security): Confirming — KMS access logs and key rotation checks are enabled for Private deployments in this flow, and audit retention extended to 90 days for exemption approvals.
emily (devex): Can we get a short changelog snippet for the release notes? Something I can paste into the weekly update.
maya: Sure — put this in the notes: "Deploy guardrails: shorter quiet window (3h), exemption CLI `/deploy-exempt`, mandatory canaries for >5% traffic changes, lowered canary alert thresholds, KMS audit retention 90d." :thumbsup:
liam (eng): ack — will use the flow for the encoder hotfix tomorrow morning.
jon (release-manager): I’ll run a quick rollout drill during the staging deploys tomorrow 10:30 PT. If anyone wants to observe or practice the exemption flow ping me.
maya: Thanks all — please read the handbook link and ask any questions here. We'll lock the policy at EOD unless major blockers appear. :lock:
file_description: internal announcement thread about deploy guardrails, quiet-window adjustments, and exemption flow for the release train
